summary: This is the Python Packaging User Guide's formal specification of the pyproject.toml file, which serves as a configuration file for packaging-related and other tools. It defines the [build-system] table (with the mandatory requires key), the [project] table holding core metadata (name as the only always-required key, with version required but static or dynamic), the [tool] table for arbitrary tool configuration, and the history of its approval through PEP 518 (May 2016) and PEP 621 (November 2020). The page is a technical spec, not a user-friendly guide.
one_line: Formal PyPA specification of the pyproject.toml file's [build-system], [project], and [tool] tables, originally defined in PEP 518 and PEP 621.
key_facts: The pyproject.toml file is written in TOML and acts as a configuration file for packaging-related tools as well as other tools.
The specification was originally defined in PEP 518 and PEP 621.
Three tables are currently specified: [build-system], [project] and [tool]; other tables are reserved for future use.
The [build-system] table's only valid key is requires, which is mandatory and must be a list of strings representing build system dependencies.
The example [build-system] table for a project built with setuptools sets requires = ["setuptools"].

If the pyproject.toml file exists but lacks the [build-system] table, the default values specified should be used; if the table is specified but missing required fields, the tool should consider it an error.
The only key required to be statically defined in the [project] table is name.
The version key is required but may be specified either statically or listed as dynamic.
Tools SHOULD normalize the project name as soon as it is read for internal consistency.
If the readme key is a string, it is a path relative to pyproject.toml to a text file; files ending in .md are assumed to be text/markdown and files ending in .rst are assumed to be text/x-rst.
A build back-end MUST raise an error if the metadata specifies name in dynamic.
Build back-ends MUST raise an error if the metadata defines a [project.entry-points.console_scripts] or [project.entry-points.gui_scripts] table.
A project can use the subtable tool.$NAME if, and only if, they own the entry for $NAME in the Cheeseshop/PyPI.
In May 2016, PEP 518 approved the initial specification with a [build-system] table containing a requires key and a [tool] table; in November 2020, PEP 621 approved the [project] table.
